title: Stage 2 actor and memory observation foundation
purpose: Define bounded versioned actor service and buffer-copy observations before any actor-work, fairness, buffer, or backpressure policy becomes forceable.
scope: This specification covers behavior-neutral per-connection actor service and selected send-side and receive-side buffer-copy observations, bounded epoch aggregation, a versioned post-service Stage 1 and Stage 2 join boundary, append-only permanent raw export, explicit missing-state handling, schema and semantic validation, and the safety gates required before actor_work_quantum or buffer_copy_coalescing. It does not define a forceable actor policy, scalar work-unit threshold, distinct conservative buffer implementation, backpressure policy, active_internal behavior, or production activation.
context: The shard already exposes aggregate queue-delay, service-time, wake, packet-run, and follow-on metrics, but it does not expose a versioned connection-attributable evidence contract or an exactly-once repost seam. Stage 2 must preserve the current drain loop and record honest primitives before proposing a quantum.
open_questions: Which cooperative transition and effect boundaries can yield while preserving exactly-once repost, timer priority, recovery, terminal drain, and buffer ownership?
How should complete shard observation coverage and runnable intervals be proven before cross-connection fairness statistics are accepted?

requirements.title: Record bounded behavior-neutral actor service evidence
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST support disabled and observe-only actor service instrumentation that records one versioned connection-attributable observation for each observed shard dispatch with monotonic service sequence, bounded wake identity, closed work kind, queue delay, complete service duration, pending work count, effect and follow-on counts, lifecycle disposition, explicit missing and saturated state, and deterministic epoch aggregation; keep sink failures diagnostic-only; preserve the legacy_current shard drain, timer, recovery, terminal, progress, and ownership behavior; and never treat scenario, payload, requested concurrency, peer, URL, application identity, event count, pending inbox depth, or queue delay as an invented production work-unit, runnable-connection, oldest-item, or deadline-lateness signal.
notes: UsefulWorkUnitsUndefined remains explicit until a reviewed work-unit vector and cooperative safe checkpoints exist.
No actor_work_quantum value is forceable or active under this requirement.

requirements.title: Record bounded behavior-neutral buffer-copy evidence
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST support disabled and observe-only connection-local buffer-copy instrumentation that records versioned legacy_current copy, reuse, formatting, combination, sent-plaintext-retention, owned path-migration retransmission-clone, and receive-segment insertion or capacity-reuse operations at existing ownership boundaries; reports logical bytes, copied bytes, source segments, requested and retained capacity, deterministic join scope, selected and applied identity, reason, latch, lifecycle, and explicit missing or invalid state; aggregates only fixed closed counters; keeps producer and sink failures diagnostic-only; preserves byte identity, ordering, packet protection, recovery, congestion, pacing, flow control, hard bounds, ownership, and exactly-once release; and does not claim a distinct conservative implementation, terminal-release correlation, retained age, pool outstanding state, forcing, shadow selection, or active behavior until each is implemented and reviewed.
notes: Only legacy_current is a real buffer-copy policy value in this slice.
The observation seam cannot be used as fabricated counterfactual policy coverage.

requirements.title: Seal unified evidence at a versioned post-service boundary
requirements.statement: The runtime MUST publish an eligible adaptive-runtime epoch only after the serviced transition, effects, follow-on measurement, actor observation, and owned work-item or connection-event resource release; record a versioned bounded boundary containing the connection epoch key, exact end tick, execution source, disposition, actor-publication state, release completion, and explicit fault or missing validity; require exact monotonic connection-observation, receive-credit, boundary, Stage 1, actor, and buffer join keys before resetting any accumulator; keep mismatched, duplicate, out-of-order, failed-sink, and partial evidence explicit and behavior-neutral; and preserve legacy_current policy application, protocol progress, recovery, cancellation, disposal, terminal work, and ownership.
notes: The connection-local joined record does not invent run, host, binary, workload, checksum, or classification provenance.
Permanent raw-file export is governed separately by REQ-QUIC-CRT-0184.

requirements.title: Export append-only unified Stage 1 and Stage 2 raw evidence
requirements.statement: The permanent raw QUIC evidence host MUST configure one connection-local accumulator as the receive-credit, all four Stage 1, actor-service, and buffer-copy evidence sink for every adaptive execution; emit one versioned raw record under one connection key only after an exact post-service join; preserve retained receive-credit and Stage 1 compatibility records without relabeling; validate unique monotonic connection epoch keys, exact observation, snapshot, boundary, Stage 1, actor, and buffer joins, exactly four Stage 1 axis records, and no more than one non-legacy applied axis per row; retain append-only source hashes, raw rows, validation counts, manifests, and export-failure records; classify any export failure as invalid_contract; and preserve legacy_current adjacent policy application and behavior-neutral evidence failure handling.
notes: Scenario, payload, requested concurrency, peer, URL, application identity, and workload provenance remain outside the production controller input contract.
The exporter is evidence infrastructure and does not authorize a Stage 2 policy value or active behavior.

requirements.title: Correlate buffer construction with authoritative terminal release
requirements.statement: Every observed buffer lifetime MUST use a compact immutable connection-local token containing only the original operation sequence, closed path, monotonic construction tick, retained capacity, and contract version; move that token with the authoritative existing owner across transfers; create a distinct token for a clone; consume a nonempty token exactly once at the existing terminal return boundary; emit a bounded release record with closed reason, released capacity, lifetime, lifecycle, and explicit missing, duplicate, mismatch, saturated, or out-of-domain validity; keep return, progress, recovery, cancellation, reset, shutdown, disposal, and ownership authoritative when evidence is disabled, rejected, or throws; and never retain object identity, add an outstanding-operation dictionary or unbounded scan, or authorize a non-legacy buffer policy before every observed owner path is verified.
notes: Receive-segment ownership is the first implementation slice; remaining owner paths stay explicit and non-forceable until separately checkpointed.
Ownership transfer is not terminal release and cannot create a duplicate completion outcome.
